brief:
Al Jazeera English reports that Israel's government is leveraging Islamophobic rhetoric to maintain backing among Western right-wing constituencies. The strategy capitalizes on growing receptiveness to anti-Muslim sentiment in conservative circles across Western democracies, particularly as traditional support faces erosion over Palestinian issues.

Netanyahu's administration frames its military and political actions within broader narratives about Islamic threat, positioning Israel as a strategic bulwark against Islamism in the Middle East. By emphasizing dangers associated with Muslim movements and populations, the government attempts to redirect Western debate away from Palestinian grievances, occupation policies, and questions of international law compliance.

The approach reflects a calculation that fears about Islam resonate more powerfully than Middle Eastern geopolitics among segments of the Western political right now receptive to such messaging.
dek: Netanyahu’s government is using anti-Muslim fear to rally a Western right increasingly receptive to its message.
title: Netanyahu government deploys anti-Muslim messaging to shore up Western support
